card.name: Verbs before 'concomitantly' or 'simultaneously'
card.fires_on: The verb or helper word (used, be, administered, done, not) right before an expected 'concomitantly', 'simultaneously' or 'at the same time'. It appears in drug-interaction sentences about two drugs given together.

modes.label: Not given together
modes.description: Helper or verb in a warning that two named drugs should not be used or given together.
modes.example: Tetrabenazine tablets and reserpine should not<< be>> used concomitantly [see Con

modes.label: Given together
modes.description: Verb after two drugs or tests when they are given or done at once.
modes.example: Sometimes a PET scan and a CT scan are<< done>> at the same time.

card.writes: It pushes toward words that mean 'at the same time' and away from ordinal words like second or third.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a sentence where two drugs or procedures are said to be given at the same time.
